question.text: Under SEBI LODR, what is a listed entity required to do when the in-house share transfer facility crosses one lakh holders?

answer.text: Either register with SEBI as a Category II Share Transfer Agent for the in-house facility, or appoint a SEBI-registered RTA
Continue operating in-house without any additional registration or appointment
Mandatorily appoint an external SEBI-registered RTA, with no other option permitted
Mandatorily register only as a Category I RTA (combined registrar and transfer agent)

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that when in-house holders exceed one lakh, the listed entity must either register with SEBI as a Category II Share Transfer Agent (to continue running the facility in-house) or appoint a SEBI-registered RTA. Both routes are explicitly available. The Trap: Saying that an external RTA must be appointed misses the in-house Category II registration option. Saying that registration is the only option misses the alternative of appointing a SEBI-registered RTA. Note: Category I covers entities providing combined registrar and transfer agent functions, while Category II covers entities providing only the transfer agent function -- which is why Category II is the relevant registration when the listed entity keeps the transfer facility in-house.
